target_customer: B2B software companies that need customers to import messy CSV and spreadsheet data
problem: Product teams spend months building and maintaining CSV importers instead of core product.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for an embeddable importer and file automation

founders.name: Andrew Luo
founders.background_notes: Role listed as CEO or CTO in different company posts

founders.name: Christina Gilbert
founders.background_notes: YC launch post says both founders worked as a product manager and an engineering manager

technical_complexity.rationale: Embeddable importers with validation are standard front end and backend work, with some difficulty in handling messy files at scale.

defensibility.rationale: Once embedded in a customer product the importer is sticky, but competitors sold similar widgets and customers could build in house.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copying found; later pages show the company repositioning toward AI agents for messy files.

market_need_then: Founders reported months of engineering lost to CSV importers in their own jobs; no dated third party demand data was found.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand was found; only a product post about a customer branding suite. Name origin and logo not documented.

outcome_analysis: OneSchema launched an embeddable CSV importer in July 2021 and raised a 6.3 million dollar round in November 2022 led by General Catalyst with Sequoia and YC. It remains active with about 20 people and has been repositioning toward AI automation for messy files. Evidence of traction beyond named customers is thin, so the story is steady but small.
notes: A 5 million dollar Series A in July 2023 appears only on geo.sig.ai and is unverified, not recorded as a round. Total raised ranges from 6.4M to 9.3M on aggregators. Competitors Flatfile, CSVBox, Dromo and Osmos were seen only in 2026 vendor posts, so the founding list is empty. Round stage label seed versus Series A varies by aggregator.
